comments.title: Include acceptance in the candidate comparison fingerprint
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include acceptance in the candidate comparison fingerprint**

When two fresh candidates receive the same brief, context files, and skills but different `acceptance` values, this code changes their effective prompts while both `context.sha256` and `skills.sha256` remain identical. The documented comparison workflow in `plugins/cstack/docs/guide/11-cli-workers.md:71` tells the coordinator to verify only those two fingerprints, so such candidates can be treated as having comparable inputs despite different success criteria, invalidating experiment results. Include `acceptance` in a comparison fingerprint or require it to be compared explicitly.

comments.title: Bind validation receipts to immutable image IDs
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind validation receipts to immutable image IDs**

Validation records only this mutable tag, and `build_image` accepts any existing image currently referenced by it. Because `validate` and `run` are separate commands, a local rebuild or retag between them can make the campaign grade with an image that never passed the red/green validation while the receipt still appears current. Record the inspected image ID or digest in the receipt and verify that exact identity before every run.

comments.title: Preserve provenance for the extracted Interrogate rules
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve provenance for the extracted Interrogate rules**

`interrogate/references/axes.md` contains the translated/adapted Interrogate synthesis rules that previously lived in the ported `interrogate/SKILL.md` (including consensus, lone-reviewer weighting, deduplication, and disagreement handling), but this entry classifies the extracted file as `original`. The existing upstream mapping now covers only the shortened SKILL and no longer records where the extracted text came from, so provenance and future upstream audits are incomplete. Record this reference as derived from the corresponding pstack/Matt source rather than as original.

comments.title: Verify fixture hashes before running scenarios
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify fixture hashes before running scenarios**

When a generated project or skill bundle changes after `cases.json` and `expectations.json` are created—for example, when a writable single-run fixture is reused—the runner loads the stored `project_sha256` and `source_sha256` but never compares them with the selected case before launching. Routing, delegation, and outcome checks can consequently pass with exit 0 for a different fixture or plugin than the expectation describes, invalidating the experiment; verify the supplied hashes before each run when those fields are present.

comments.title: Reject directory symlinks from provenance trees
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject directory symlinks from provenance trees**

When a project or bundle contains a directory symlink, `os.walk` leaves it in `names` but does not descend into it, and this loop hashes only `filenames`; `verify-behavior.py` has the same blind spot. Retargeting the symlink or changing files beneath its external target therefore leaves `project_sha256`/`source_sha256` unchanged even though the native task can read different code, silently invalidating experiment provenance. Reject directory symlinks for every hashed tree or include their effective contents in both implementations.

comments.title: Include executable modes in provenance hashes
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include executable modes in provenance hashes**

If a project or bundle executable is changed from mode 0755 to 0644 after expectations are generated, both tree-hash implementations still produce the same digest because they serialize only its path and contents. The native task can no longer execute that file, so the provenance gate accepts a materially different input; include the relevant file type and permission bits in both the generator and verifier hashes.

comments.title: Bind scenario inputs to the generated provenance
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind scenario inputs to the generated provenance**

The generated provenance authenticates the project, bundle, and skill but not the execution-defining case fields created immediately above, so editing `cases.json` after generation—for example replacing `prompt`/`prompts` or changing `sandbox`—still passes `verify_provenance` and launches a materially different experiment under the original expectations. Because the receipt has no trusted digest of the original case configuration, the altered result cannot be tied back to the generated task; include a canonical digest of the prompts and relevant execution settings in the expectation and verify it before launch.

comments.title: Reject special files instead of omitting them from provenance
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject special files instead of omitting them from provenance**

When a project or bundle contains a FIFO, Unix socket, device, or another non-regular filesystem entry, `is_file()` is false and the entry is silently skipped, so adding, removing, or replacing it leaves the v2 digest unchanged. A native task can still observe or interact with that path—potentially changing its behavior or blocking on a FIFO—while `verify_provenance` accepts the tree as identical; reject unsupported entry types explicitly or encode them in both hash implementations.

comments.title: Include Git state in project provenance
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include Git state in project provenance**

For generated scenarios that depend on repository state, such as `interrogate_current_work_*` and `interrogate_partial_set_*`, this verification trusts a tree hash that excludes `.git`. Unstaging a file or moving `HEAD` changes what `git diff --cached` presents to the native task without changing any working-tree bytes, so the original `project_sha256` still passes while a materially different review is executed. Bind the relevant index, HEAD, and refs—or a canonical Git diff/status snapshot—into the generated and verified provenance.

comments.title: Encode directory entries in tree hashes
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Encode directory entries in tree hashes**

The new hash format validates directory symlinks but never serializes regular directory paths or their modes; it hashes only files below them. Adding or removing an empty directory, or changing a directory's permissions, therefore leaves both project and bundle digests unchanged even though the native task can observe the difference and tools may require that directory to exist or be writable. Include directory entries in both hash implementations.

comments.title: Encode file-symlink targets in provenance
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Encode file-symlink targets in provenance**

When a regular-file symlink is retargeted to another file with identical bytes and mode, `stat()` and `read_bytes()` follow the link, so its v2 digest remains unchanged even though a native task can observe a different link target (for example through `readlink` or a Git diff) and writes now affect another file. Moreover, single runs retain the symlink while repeated runs materialize it via `copytree`, giving the same attested scenario different filesystem semantics. Reject file symlinks or include their type and target in both hash implementations while preserving them consistently during repeats.

comments.title: Preserve receipts when post-run hashing fails
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve receipts when post-run hashing fails**

When the native task creates a FIFO, socket, device, or directory symlink in its workspace, this new rejection is reached by the post-run `tree_hash` call at line 930. That call is outside `run_case`'s protected `try`, so the completed turn never produces a result, `summary.json` is not updated with its evidence, and all remaining cases are aborted. Keep rejecting unsupported entries during preflight, but record a post-run hash error as an explicit result-level evidence gap instead of discarding the native result.

comments.title: Include in-progress Git state in the digest
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include in-progress Git state in the digest**

When a fixture is mid-merge or mid-cherry-pick, this default `for-each-ref` listing skips root pseudorefs such as `MERGE_HEAD`; the [Git documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-for-each-ref) exposes `--include-root-refs` specifically for including root refs and pseudorefs. Consequently, changing or removing `MERGE_HEAD` leaves `git_sha256` unchanged while Git changes from an in-progress operation to a clean state, so provenance can accept materially different review input. Hash the relevant pseudorefs/operation metadata separately, or reject fixtures with an operation in progress.

comments.title: Allow provenance hashing on unborn branches
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow provenance hashing on unborn branches**

For a valid repository created with `git init` but not yet committed, `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` exits nonzero and this tuple permits only code 0, so both the scenario generator and verifier reject the fixture as inaccessible before hashing its index or running the case. Git explicitly supports this state—the [Git glossary](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary) defines an unborn branch as `HEAD` pointing to a branch with no commit—so encode the head OID as `null` while retaining `head_ref`, refs, and index state rather than rejecting new repositories.

comments.title: Reject or hash nested Git repositories
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject or hash nested Git repositories**

When a fixture contains an independent repository in a subdirectory, both hashers prune its `.git` directory while these commands snapshot only the outer repository. I verified that switching the nested repository between two commits with the same tree leaves both `project_sha256` and `git_sha256` unchanged, even though commands such as `git -C nested log` expose different review input; Git defines `HEAD` as the current checked-out branch tip in the [Git glossary](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary). Either reject nested repositories or include each nested Git snapshot in the digest.
